QF.id: SIA Logic Model for Social Programs_2

question.text: Swasth Bharat Trust has asked Mr. Arjun Desai (Cost Accountant, SIA on empanelment waitlist) to comment on the order of elements in its Logic Model. Which of the following represents the correct flow as per the chapter?

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per Ch 4.3, the Logic Model flows from Inputs (resources) -> Activities (tasks) -> Outputs (deliverables) -> Outcomes (immediate/intermediate changes) -> Impact (long-term consequences). Option B captures this causal chain. Note: the chapter lists the Logic Model flow starting from Impact at the TOP when describing the hierarchy, but the CAUSAL flow (how value is created) runs from Inputs upward. **The Trap:** A reverses the chain (it lists the hierarchy top-down, not the causal flow). C and B scramble the sequence — common trap for candidates who memorise words without the causal logic. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-tested in XXIII Ch 5 (Social Impact Measurement) and referenced by SAS-200/400/500/1100/1300. X-A Investment Adviser also tests this for CSR Section 135 project evaluation. **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** When you draw the 5-layer pyramid for a new engagement, write the causal direction (bottom-up) on one side and the accountability direction (top-down, Impact drives design) on the other. Keeps you from conflating the two.
